newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Trade Minister says has resigned from cabinet.
newsitem.headline: Czech Trade Minister says has resigned from cabinet.

text.p: Czech Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy told a meeting of the leaders of his Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA) party early Saturday morning that he has resigned from the cabinet, the Czech news agency CTK reported.

The leaders of the other two parties in the ruling coalition, the Christian Democratic Union (KDU) and the Civic Democratic Party (ODS), are also holding meetings this weekend to discuss a cabinet reshuffle aimed at reversing a fall in support for the government.
Last Wednesday, Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus agreed with coalition partners that cabinet changes were needed to deal with a downturn in the economy which has sapped confidence in the government.
The other likely candidate to leave the cabinet is Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik, a member of the Civic Democratic Party (ODS), though other ministers are also expected to go.

The expected reshuffle has been given greater urgency by the battering the Czech crown has received in the foreign exchange markets. On Thursday, the crown reached a record low six percent below the central bank's mark/dollar parity level.
But the crown rallied strongly on Friday to a level 0.8 percent below parity, helped by central bank intervention.
CTK reported that the ODA, which is meeting in the southern city of Trebon, has called for party leader Michael Zantovsky to take a post in the cabinet.
Zantovsky, who became ODA leader earlier this year after returning from his former post as ambassador to Washington, has been tipped for Defence or Foreign Affairs.
